response: Yes, complex coronary lesions are more frequent in patients with diabetes mellitus. Research has shown that complex coronary lesions, such as bifurcation and ostial lesions, are significantly more common in diabetic patients than in nondiabetic patients. Additionally, greater age and the presence of diabetes mellitus (DM) are independent predictors for these complex lesions, which may help explain the poor prognosis of coronary artery disease among diabetic patients.
